text: MySQL's installation is deliberately lighter than Oracle's, which is part of why it spread so widely through web hosting and application stacks. This lesson walks the real install flow, on Linux with a package manager and with Docker.

On Debian and Ubuntu-family systems, MySQL installs through the standard package manager, which registers a systemd service. On a fresh install, check the install log for a temporary root password some distributions generate automatically.

Running MySQL in a container with Docker is now a completely normal pattern for local development and increasingly for production. The named volume is what makes the data survive a container restart — without it, removing the container destroys the database with it.

mysql_secure_installation is the script every fresh install should run before anything touches it. It sets the root password, removes anonymous user accounts, disables remote root login, removes the test database, and reloads the privilege tables so the changes take effect immediately.
A quick SELECT VERSION() confirms the server accepted the connection and the client can reach it. Next up: MySQL's configuration files and system variables — my.cnf, SHOW VARIABLES, and SET GLOBAL.
